files.lesson.md: --- order: 1 unit: integers node: AC9M7N07 n1 assumes: [AC9M6N01 n1, AC9M6N01 n2] title: Comparing integers summary: On a number line, the number further left is less. So −7 is less than −2, even though 7 is more than 2. language: maths voice: { name: af_heart, speed: 1.1 } connection: winter-minimums # data/connections/maths.yml hook: "On a cold morning Thredbo is at −9 °C and Canberra at −3 °C (made-up temperatures for the task). Which is colder, and which number is bigger?" app: command: node "$REPO_ROOT/tools/serve.mjs" "$REPO_ROOT/dist/_playground-board" 8160 url: http://127.0.0.1:8160/index.html readySelector: "#sl-a" layout: full explainPicture: { ref: line.yml#explain-pic, caption: "$-7$ is further left than $-2$, so $-7 < -2$." } explainClip: query: { code: "@line.yml#explain", fresh: 1, id: explain } caption: "Further left is less" say: "On a number line, further left is less." clip: - caption: { text: "−3 is left of 2, so −3 < 2.", say: "Negative three is left of two, so it is less." } - wait: 300 - caption: { text: "Move A to −7 and B to −2.", say: "Now move A to negative seven, and B to negative two." } - click: Make a smaller - click: Make a smaller - click: Make a smaller - click: Make a smaller - click: Make b smaller - click: Make b smaller - click: Make b smaller - click: Make b smaller - caption: { text: "−7 is further left, so −7 < −2.", say: "Negative seven is further left, so it is less than negative two." } - expect: { selector: "#nlcompare", contains: "−7 < −2" } - wait: 1000 --- Numbers below zero are **negative**: $-1, -2, -3$ and so on. Together with zero and the positive whole numbers they are the **integers**. On a number line, negatives sit to the left of zero, with $-1$ next to zero. So which of two integers is less, and how do you write that down? The signs are $<$ ("is less than") and $>$ ("is greater than"). ## Predict: which is greater? ```step stage: predict insight: "Committing to an answer for −7 and −2 before using the line makes the board a test of their idea about negatives, not a demonstration." check: type: predict q: "Which is greater, $-7$ or $-2$?" options: - "$-2$" - "$-7$, because 7 is more than 2" - "Neither: they are both negative, so they are equal" - "You cannot compare two negative numbers" actual: "−2 is greater. On the number line −2 is to the right of −7: further right is greater. −7 is further below zero, so it is less." ``` Think of temperatures: is $-7$ °C or $-2$ °C warmer? ## Run: two points on the line ```step stage: run insight: "Placing −7 and −2 and reading the sentence shows the rule: further left is less, for negatives as well as positives." try: { playground: board, starter: "line.yml#run", height: 380 } check: { type: board, text: "Put $A$ at $-7$ and $B$ at $-2$. Was your prediction right?", when: "x(A) = -7 and x(B) = -2" } ``` Move $A$ with slider $a$ and $B$ with slider $b$ (or the − and + buttons). The board writes the comparison under the line. Try a few pairs first: two positives, a positive and a negative, then $-7$ and $-2$. ## Investigate: further left is less ```step stage: investigate insight: "Further left is less, so the order of negatives runs the opposite way to their sizes without the sign: −8 is less than −2. Ari's mistake orders by the size alone." tasks: - check: type: question q: "Which is true?" options: ["$-5 < -1$", "$-5 > -1$", "$-5 = -1$"] answer: 0 feedback: [null, "Find both on the line: −5 is four places to the left of −1. Further left is less.", "They are at different places on the line."] explain: "−5 is further left than −1, so −5 < −1." - check: type: bug code: "working.txt#ari" text: "Ari puts four numbers in order. Click the line where the reasoning goes wrong." answer: 3 fault: logic misconception: negative-magnitude explain: "Line 3: 8 is bigger than 2, but −8 is further below zero than −2, so −8 is less. The order is −8, −2, 0, 3." - check: type: sort q: "Less than $-3$, or greater than $-3$?" options: ["Less than −3", "Greater than −3"] items: - ["−6", "Less than −3"] - ["−1", "Greater than −3"] - ["0", "Greater than −3"] - ["−10", "Less than −3"] - ["2", "Greater than −3"] - ["−4", "Less than −3", "−4 is one place left of −3."] ``` ### Ordering on the line Here is how to put integers in order, using where each one sits on the number line. ```worked -2, \; -8, \; 3, \; 0 :: Put these in order from least to greatest. \text{place each on the line} :: Negatives go left of zero: $-2$ is 2 left, $-8$ is 8 left. -8 \text{ is furthest left} :: Furthest left is least, so $-8$ comes first. -8, \; -2, \; 0, \; 3 :: Read the line from left to right. -8 < -2 :: Between two negatives, the one further from zero is less. ``` ### Find the mistake Read Ari's working one line at a time. Which line orders the numbers by their size alone? ### Either side of −3 Sort each number: is it less than $-3$, or greater? ## Modify: one change at a time ```step stage: modify insight: "One change at a time: a number between two negatives, the same idea in temperatures, then the edge case where the number further from zero is the smaller one." try: { playground: board, starter: "line.yml#between", height: 420 } tasks: - starter: "line.yml#between" hint: ["Which way from −4 is less: left or right?", "Go left of −4, but not as far as −8."] check: { type: board, text: "Drag $P$ to a number that is less than $-4$ and greater than $-8$.", when: "x(P) < -4 and x(P) > -8", explain: "−5, −6 or −7: left of −4 and right of −8." } - starter: "line.yml#weather" hint: ["Warmer is further right. Is it above or below zero?", "Right of Canberra (−3), but still left of 0."] check: { type: board, text: "Drag $P$ to a temperature warmer than Canberra but still below zero.", when: "x(P) > -3 and x(P) < 0", explain: "−2 °C or −1 °C: further right than −3, still left of 0." } - starter: "line.yml#below" hint: "Which way is less: left or right? Is zero left or right of −1?" check: { type: board, text: "Drag $P$ to a number less than $-1$. Then try zero: is it less or greater than $-1$?", when: "x(P) < -1", explain: "Any number left of −1 is less: −2, −3 and so on. Zero is to the right, so 0 > −1." } - check: type: question q: "Edge case: $-10$ is further from zero than $-1$. Which is greater?" options: ["$-1$", "$-10$, because it is further from zero", "They are equal: both are negative"] answer: 0 feedback: [null, "Further from zero tells you the size without the sign. Further left on the line is less.", "Both being negative does not make them equal: they are 9 places apart on the line."] explain: "−1 > −10. −10 is further from zero, but it is further left, so it is less." ``` ### Between two negatives Each task changes one thing. First: drag $P$ to a number between $-8$ and $-4$. ### Temperatures The same idea in degrees. Warmer means further right. ### Zero and the negatives Zero is greater than every negative number. ### Further from zero When is the number further from zero the smaller one? ## Practise: compare and order ```step stage: practise insight: "Comparing with < and >, ordering, and a context, mixed; the review question keeps locating integers from Year 6 fresh." tasks: - check: type: question q: "Which sign goes in the gap? $-6 \\;\\square\\; -9$" options: ["$>$", "$<$"] answer: 0 feedback: [null, "Find both: −9 is further left, so −9 is the smaller one. The sign opens towards the greater number."] explain: "−6 > −9: −6 is to the right of −9." smaller: check: { type: question, q: "Which of $-6$ and $-9$ is further left on the number line?", options: ["$-9$", "$-6$"], answer: 0, feedback: [null, "Find both on the line. Which one has the other to its right?"], explain: "−9 is further left. Further left is less, so the sign opens towards −6." } - check: type: question q: "Which list is in order from least to greatest?" options: ["$-9, -4, 0, 2, 5$", "$-4, -9, 0, 2, 5$", "$0, -4, -9, 2, 5$"] answer: 0 feedback: [null, "Is −4 less than −9? Find both on the line.", "Negatives are less than zero, so they come before it."] explain: "Left to right on the line: −9, −4, 0, 2, 5." - check: type: question q: "At 6 am it was $-5$ °C in Cooma and $-8$ °C in Perisher. Which was colder?" options: ["Perisher", "Cooma"] answer: 0 feedback: [null, "Colder is further left. Which of −5 and −8 is further left?"] explain: "−8 < −5, so Perisher was colder." - check: type: answer q: "Review: what number is 4 places to the left of 1 on a number line?" answer: "-3" feedback: - ["5", "That is 4 to the right. Left is towards the negatives."] - ["3", "Count left from 1: 0, −1, −2, −3."] explain: "From 1, four places left: 0, −1, −2, −3." ``` ### Which sign? ### In order ### Colder ### Review ## Make: a surprising pair ```step stage: make insight: "Building a pair where the less number is the one further from zero reverses the lesson: from the rule to an example that shows it." try: { playground: board, starter: "line.yml#make", height: 420 } hint: ["P must be further left than Q.", "Try putting P below zero, further from zero than Q is: P at −6 and Q at −2, or Q at 3."] check: { type: board, text: "Place $P$ and $Q$ so that $P < Q$, but $P$ is further from zero than $Q$.", when: "x(P) < x(Q) and x(P) + x(Q) < 0", explain: "P is left of Q, so P < Q, and further from zero: it must be a negative, such as P = −6 and Q = −2 (or Q = 3)." } ``` Find a pair where the less number has the bigger size without its sign. The sentence under the line tells you which is less. Stretch: write three temperatures below zero, then put them in order from warmest to coldest. ## Make: a week of frosts on paper ```step stage: make insight: "Ordering five temperatures forces the misconception into the open: the biggest-looking number is the coldest night, not the warmest." hint: ["Draw a number line from −10 to 5 and mark each night on it.", "Further left is colder."] check: type: reasoning paper: true q: "Overnight lows in Canberra one winter week, in °C (made up for the task): Mon $-3$, Tue $-8$, Wed $2$, Thu $-1$, Fri $-5$. Put the nights in order from coldest to warmest, and name the coldest and the warmest." steps: - ["Mark $-8$, $-5$, $-3$, $-1$ and $2$ on a number line", "temperatures are numbers on a line, with zero in the middle"] - ["$-8$ is the furthest left, so Tuesday is the coldest", "further left is less, and less is colder"] - ["From left to right: $-8$, $-5$, $-3$, $-1$, $2$", "reading left to right goes from least to greatest"] - ["Coldest is Tuesday ($-8$ °C), warmest is Wednesday ($2$ °C)", "Wednesday is the only night above zero"] picks: - step: 2 q: "Why is $-8$ colder than $-1$?" options: - "$-8$ is further left on the line, so it is less" - "8 is bigger than 1, so $-8$ is the bigger temperature" - "A negative number is colder the closer it is to zero" answer: 0 feedback: [null, "8 is bigger than 1, but the minus sign turns it round: −8 is 8 below zero.", "It is the other way. The further below zero, the colder."] - step: 3 q: "Why does $-5$ come before $-3$ in the order?" options: - "$-5$ is to the left of $-3$, so it is less" - "5 is more than 3, so it should come last" - "It does not matter: both are negative" answer: 0 feedback: [null, "Order by position on the line, not by the number without its sign.", "It matters. Negatives are in order too: the one further left is less."] criteria: - "I marked every night on a number line before I ordered them." - "I put the one furthest left first." - "I checked that my list goes up from left to right." explain: "On the line, −8 is furthest left, so it is the coldest, and 2 is furthest right, so it is the warmest. In order: −8, −5, −3, −1, 2. A bigger number without its sign means colder when the number is negative." ``` Do this one in your book, not on the screen. The temperatures are made up for the task, but the question is real: weather reports list frosty lows, and you have to say which night was coldest. Mark the nights on a line, then order them. The page marks the two reasons you pick. **Also used in** - **Weather.** Overnight lows, and heights above or below sea level, are compared on a line with zero in the middle. - **Buildings.** Car park levels below ground are negative: level −3 is lower than level −1. - **Money.** An account at −\$50 owes more than one at −\$10, though 50 is the bigger number. ```teacher summary: Students place integers on a number line, find that further left is less (so −7 < −2), and compare and order integers with < and > (AC9M7N07, node 1). time: 40 timing: Predict and Run 8 min · Investigate 12 min · Modify 10 min · Practise and Make 10 min goals: - I can put a set of integers, including negatives, in order from least to greatest. - I can write a comparison between two integers with < or >. - I can explain why −10 is less than −1, even though 10 is more than 1. struggle: Seeing −8 as less than −2 when 8 looks bigger than 2. Ask "which is colder?" and have them mark both on the line before they decide. before: > Do the Run board and the Make task yourself first. Students should be able to find negative numbers on a number line (Year 6) and know what a temperature below zero means. The one idea of the lesson is "further left is less". The common mistake is to compare negatives by their size without the sign (−8 > −2 because 8 > 2), and it is planted only after the method, in Ari's working. The lesson says "further from zero" for size without the sign, not "absolute value". The primer has the word if you want it. running: - "Predict: take a show of hands. Students who chose −7 usually say 7 is bigger. Do not correct it yet: the board will." - "Run: ask students to try two positives first, then a positive and a negative, then −7 and −2. Ask: what decides which is less every time?" - "Investigate: model the worked example live. Draw a line on the board, place −2, −8, 3 and 0 one at a time, saying 'left of zero, 8 places' and so on, then read left to right. Reveal the prepared lines afterwards to compare." - "Modify: each task changes one thing. Before the temperature task ask: which way is warmer?" - "Practise: the sign question plants the reversed sign. A student who picks < can place both on the line and say which is further left." - "Make: collect a few pairs. Ask: could P be positive? (No: a positive further from zero than Q would be greater than Q.)" - "Paper: the week of frosts is worked in books; the page marks two reasons (why −8 is colder than −1, why −5 comes before −3) and has no number answer. Books out, then look for every night marked on a line before ordering." stuck: - see: A student says −8 is greater than −2. ask: Which is colder, −8 °C or −2 °C? fix: Place both on the line. Further left is less, and −8 is further left. Say it as 'eight below zero' and 'two below zero'. - see: A student puts negatives in the order −1, −2, −3 when asked for least to greatest. ask: Which of these is furthest left on the line? fix: "Point at the line and read it from left to right: −3, −2, −1." - see: A student mixes up < and >. ask: Which number is greater? Which way does the wide end of the sign face? fix: "The wide end faces the greater number: −6 > −9 reads '−6 is greater than −9'." stretch: "Which is greater, −0.5 or −5? Place both on the line. Then: is there an integer between −3 and −2?" support: "Use the Run board for every comparison: set a and b to the two numbers and read the sentence. A paper number line from −10 to 10 on every desk helps." leads: > Next: adding and subtracting integers, as moves along the same line. Where it leads: plotting points in all four quadrants, reading graphs with negative values, and comparing negative fractions and decimals (AC9M7N04). exit: q: "Put in order from least to greatest: 4, −6, 0, −1, −10." a: −10, −6, −1, 0, 4. explain: > On a number line, the number **further left is less**. That is true below zero too. $-7$ is further left than $-2$, so $-7 < -2$ ("$-7$ is less than $-2$"), even though 7 is more than 2. Think of temperatures: $-7$ °C is colder than $-2$ °C. To put integers in order, place each on the line and read from left to right. Zero is greater than every negative number. ```

# Number line boards for "Comparing integers". Dragged points land on whole numbers.

# region: run
widget: numberline
range: -10, 10
slider a: -10, 10, 0
slider b: -10, 10, 0
point A: a
point B: b
compare: A, B
# endregion

# region: explain
widget: numberline
range: -10, 10
slider a: -10, 10, -3
slider b: -10, 10, 2
point A: a
point B: b
compare: A, B
# endregion

# region: explain-pic
widget: numberline
range: -10, 10
point A: -7
point B: -2
compare: A, B
# endregion

# region: between
widget: numberline
range: -10, 10
point A: -8
point B: -4
point P: 0, drag
# endregion

# region: weather
widget: numberline
range: -12, 6
context: Temperature (°C)
point C: -3, Canberra
point T: -9, Thredbo
point P: 3, drag
# endregion

# region: below
widget: numberline
range: -10, 10
point A: -1
point P: 0, drag
compare: A, P
# endregion

# region: make
widget: numberline
range: -10, 10
point P: 2, drag
point Q: 5, drag
compare: P, Q
# endregion

# region: ari
Put these in order from least to greatest: −2, −8, 3, 0
The numbers without signs are 2, 8, 3 and 0.
8 is the biggest of those, so −8 is the greatest negative.
Least to greatest: −2, −8, 0, 3
